reviews.review:
[b] First, let’s talk gameplay [/b]
It’s kind of hard to describe how the game actually plays because I haven’t played anything quite like it. You play grid-based tennis with extra mechanics? I guess? Outside of the primary gameplay loop, it plays like any roguelike worth its salt, with a synergistic, emergent combo system similar to Balatro and Nubby. There are some obvious limbs (read: cards) and tattoos (read: relics/jokers) that feel a bit centralizing, but overall it’s pretty balanced. The way certain traits become game-breaking differs from run to run, so builds don’t end up feeling the same.

[b] Next is presentation and user experience. [/b]
The presentation is very unique yet still comprehensible. It’s got that abstract look without feeling like it’s trying too hard. That said, I do think the novelty wears off a bit as you keep playing but that’s more due to the nature of roguelikes. After your 50th run, you won’t be as impressed by how the game looks. Overall though, I love it!

The user experience is also nearly flawless. I never feel lost, and everything feels like it has a purpose. One criticism I have is the lack of a codex to remind you what each limb does. It’s not essential, there aren’t that many limbs to keep track of but it would be a nice QoL addition. Still, very solid in this department.


[b]What really hits the spot for me is the content size.[/b]
I don’t know why, but I really dislike when a game “overstays its welcome.” I like Balatro, Inscryption, and Slay the Spire, but I don’t love that I basically have to become a hermit for a week to feel satisfied. I get that the appeal of roguelikes is drowning yourself in experimentation and finding new builds but at some point, I just want to play something else or touch some grass.

This is where Torso Tennis shines compared to other roguelikes. It nails that perfect content size: big enough to dive deep for a couple of days, but not so big that you’re stuck drowning in it for weeks. You take a bite, want seconds and thirds, compliment the chef, and then move on to something else. Call me crazy, but I think this is what a healthy relationship with a game looks like.


[b]And the best part?[/b]
You can get this healthy, delicious meal for 7.50 AUD or 4.99 USD. I’ve played Indie games three times the price that I dread touching just to “get my money’s worth.” I wish more games released with this kind of price and content size. Honestly, I would’ve paid double if I could.

100% recommend!
